ledger.note: 1567: Hesse-Kassel is created. 'The state was created in 1567 when the Landgraviate of Hesse was divided upon the death of Philip I'; William IV inherited the northern half and Kassel.

region.text: the northern half of the Landgraviate and Kassel

ledger.note: 1583: the Rheinfels line dies out. 'The Rheinfels branch died out in 1583 and was shared between the other three' (footnote); the Landgraviate of Hesse page says it was 'incorporated into Hesse-Kassel'.

region.text: the Rheinfels lands on the Middle Rhine

ledger.note: 1604: Hesse-Marburg falls to Kassel. 'Hesse-Kassel expanded in 1604 when Maurice, Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel inherited the Landgraviate of Hesse-Marburg'; Hesse-Darmstadt disputed it.

1627: Maurice abdicates after ceding land. 'After being forced to cede some of his territories to Hesse-Darmstadt, Maurice abdicated in 1627 in favour of his son William V.' The page does not name the land; Marburg is the Upper Hesse city the two houses fought over.

region.text: the Marburg lands ceded to Hesse-Darmstadt

ledger.note: 1648: Marburg returns to Kassel. 'The conflict was finally settled on the eve of the 1648 Peace of Westphalia. Large parts of the disputed Upper Hesse territory, including Marburg, fell to the elder Kassel line' (Hesse-Darmstadt page); Darmstadt kept Giessen and Biedenkopf.

1648: Westphalia rewards Hesse-Kassel. 'At the Peace of Westphalia in 1648, Hesse-Kassel was further rewarded with most of the County of Schaumburg' and the secularized Hersfeld Abbey (the page gives no separate date for the abbey).

region.text: most of the County of Schaumburg (Rinteln) and Hersfeld Abbey

ledger.note: 1736: Hanau-Münzenberg comes to Hesse-Kassel. 'Count Johann Reinhard III, the last male member of the Hanau family died in 1736'; Hanau-Münzenberg went to the Landgraviate of Hesse-Kassel under the 1643 succession treaty (Hanau-Lichtenberg to Darmstadt).

region.text: the county of Hanau-Münzenberg round Hanau

ledger.note: 1760: the French hold Marburg. 'The French captured Marburg in Hesse'; a siege of Kassel failed in March 1761 and 'his Brunswick allies captured the key town of Göttingen and compounded this by taking Cassel' in the 1762 campaigns.

region.text: Hessian towns held by the French: Marburg, and Kassel until the allies retook it

ledger.note: 1763: Hesse's occupied towns are returned. The page says Hanover's and Hesse's occupied towns were returned under the Treaty of Paris in 1763.
1801: Hesse cedes land to France. 'In 1801, Hesse was forced to cede land to Revolutionary France'; the page names no land (the Rheinfels lands on the left Rhine bank are the researcher's reading).

region.text: land ceded to Revolutionary France, probably the Rheinfels lands

ledger.note: 1803: Hesse-Kassel becomes an Electorate. Infobox 'Raised to Electorate: 1803'; 'in 1803 it was compensated with land around the former Electorate of Mainz'; William I was dispossessed by Napoleon in 1806 and Kassel became the capital of the Kingdom of Westphalia.

region.text: the landgraviate, continued as the Electorate of Hesse

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (4 pages opened for this dossier, with the Landgraviate of Hesse page shared with the sibling dossier). New state: Cliopatria's 'Electorate of Hesse' starts only in 1803.

SHAPES ARE RADIUS READINGS: Kassel 44 km (matching the footnote's 6,100 km2), Marburg 30 km, Rinteln 22 km for Schaumburg, Bad Hersfeld 18 km for the abbey, Hanau 22 km, St. Goar 14 km for the Rheinfels share. Gazetteer names wanted: 'Marburg', 'Hanau', 'Rinteln', 'Bad Hersfeld', 'St. Goar'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) The Imperial invasion of Hesse-Kassel in the Thirty Years' War is undated on the page. (2) The Treaty of Westphalia's Hersfeld clause is undated on the page (placed in 1648). (3) The page does not name the land ceded in 1627 or 1801; Marburg and the Rheinfels lands are readings. (4) Cadet lines (Hesse-Rotenburg, Philippsthal, Barchfeld) and the 1736 Hanau-Münzenberg inheritance details are not on the Kassel page; the Hanau page supplied 1736. (5) Rulers not given: the page lists only William IV by name; no ruler list was opened. (6) The 1801 land ceded and the French 1806-1813 Kingdom of Westphalia belong to the electorate dossier (eu-20).
